primary_reference.title: 3D-IDS: Doubly Disentangled Dynamic Intrusion Detection
key_points: Existing NIDS methods show inconsistent F1 across attack types and especially weak unknown-attack detection.
Method combines two-step feature disentanglement, memory-based representation learning, and dynamic graph diffusion for spatiotemporal aggregation.
Explainability is claimed as a benefit of disentanglement.

supporting_references.title: E-GraphSAGE: A Graph Neural Network based Intrusion Detection System for IoT
key_points: Flow data can be naturally represented as graphs with endpoints as nodes and flows as edges.
Topological information plus edge features are useful for intrusion detection.

supporting_references.title: BSNet: Bi-Similarity Network for Few-shot Fine-grained Image Classification
key_points: Multiple similarity spaces can improve few-shot generalization through more discriminative fused representations.

supporting_references.title: DisenLink
key_points: Disentangled factors can help represent heterophilic graph structure and latent relational causes.

implications_for_task: Need per-attack consistency analysis rather than only overall metrics.
Need at least one graph-aware model or graph-derived aggregation step.
Need explicit few-shot experiment and interpretability artifact.
